summary: EFB map displays: VFR, low and high IFR maps with real airspace, a taxi route you click on the ground chart, a flight and airport search with Go to, and a cleaner Flight Deck.
releaseNotes: Map displays: VFR, IFR Low and IFR High vector maps, with terrain, airways and labels drawn for pilots.
Airspaces layer: controlled and special-use airspace from FAA data and your simulator, with class and altitude limits.
Taxi route: turn it on, click taxiways on the ground chart, and a green guide line follows the taxiways, listing them in order.
Search flights, airports and navaids from the Flight Deck; Go to takes the map there and tracks a flight, even one elsewhere on the network.
EFB airport ground chart: a Find taxiway search highlights a taxiway and zooms to it.
Your aircraft is a magenta arrowhead pointing along your track; the aircraft icon is still available in Settings.
The route draws as a cased line with boxed ident tags, leg distance and track labels, and chart symbols for each point.
Ground charts use chart colours, show stand numbers and name each taxiway once.
Navaids use enroute chart colours on every map: blue VORs (boxed with DME), purple NDBs, grey fixes and teal airports.
3D views place the trail and altitude stalk at the aircraft's exact height.
The EFB airport ground chart no longer stays on Loading: it reads the map tiles first and adds the bridge's data when it arrives.
Taxiway labels no longer keep a leading Taxiway or Twy.
The Flight Deck map runs to the top edge: the top bar is replaced by a search panel at the top left.
Map settings are grouped into Map, Weather, Aeronautical and Traffic sections.
Shared fonts, spacing and top bar across the Live, Logbook and Weather pages.
